facts.statement: Anabisetia was named by Argentine paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Jorge Orlando Calvo in 2002.
facts.quote: Argentine paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Jorge Orlando Calvo named Anabisetia in 2002.

facts.statement: The genus name Anabisetia honors Ana Maria Biset, an influential Argentine archaeologist from Neuquén Province.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the late Ana Maria Biset, an influential archeologist from Neuquén Province in Argentina, where the remains of this animal were found.

facts.statement: Anabisetia lived in a swamp environment from approximately 95 to 92 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The sediments in this formation preserve a swamp which existed from the late Cenomanian through early Turonian stages of the Late Cretaceous Period, or about 95 to 92 million years ago.

facts.statement: Anabisetia was a small, bipedal herbivore about 2 meters long.
facts.quote: It was a small bipedal herbivore, around 2 m long.

facts.statement: Anabisetia possessed the largest acromial process ever found in Euornithopoda.
facts.quote: The shoulder blade had an extension on its upper lower rim, the acromial process, that relatively was the largest ever found in the Euornithopoda.

facts.statement: The ilium of Anabisetia has a front blade representing more than half the total length and extending in front of the prepubis.
facts.quote: En la pelvis, el ilion tiene una hoja frontal que representa más de la mitad de la longitud total y está extendido frente al prepubis.

facts.statement: In 2015, Anabisetia was classified within the clade Elasmaria alongside other Antarctic and Patagonian ornithopods.
facts.quote: However, in 2015, both taxa were found to be part of the clade Elasmaria along with other Antarctic and Patagonian ornithopods.

facts.statement: Anabisetia is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: infraordo: Iguanodontia

facts.statement: Anabisetia belongs to the unranked family Elasmaria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Elasmaria

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH 74 includes a partial braincase, lower jaw bones, complete forelimb and hindlimb, and vertebrae from all spinal sections.
facts.quote: The holotype, MCF-PVPH 74, is the most complete of the four. It consists of fragmentary skull material, including a partial braincase and both dentary (lower jaw) bones, as well as a complete forelimb from shoulder to hand, a complete hindlimb and foot, and representative vertebrae from all sections of the spinal column.

facts.statement: Combined, the four known specimens provide a nearly complete skeleton of Anabisetia except for the skull.
facts.quote: When all four specimens are considered, the skeleton is more or less completely known except for the skull.

facts.statement: It is debated how precisely Anabisetia can be classified due to the lack of skull material, though it is thought to be closely related to Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: This dinosaur is thought to be closely related to another Patagonian ornithopod, Gasparinisaura, although the lack of skull material makes it difficult to place with precision.

facts.statement: Anabisetia had a small head with teeth specialized for grinding vegetation.
facts.quote: La cabeza era pequeña, con dientes especializados en moler la vegetación.

facts.statement: Researchers initially debated whether early South American ornithopods like Gasparinisaura represented an endemic lineage or were related to North American species.
facts.quote: Cuando Coria y Salgado, en 1996 descubrieron a Gasparinisaura, propusieron que pertenecía a un linaje endémico de Sudamérica muchos no estuvieron de acuerdo

facts.statement: The discovery of Anabisetia in older sediments confirmed the existence of a distinct lineage of South American ornithopods.
facts.quote: Cuando se encontró en Anabisetia en sedimentos más antiguos a esta migración, quedó confirmada que existió un linaje propio de ornitópodos sudamericanos

facts.statement: Anabisetia is classified within Iguanodontia based on parallel tooth margins and specific features in the ilium and femur.
facts.quote: Basados en los márgenes paralelos de los dientes, particularidades en el ilion y en el fémur, es colocado dentro de Iguanodontia, junto con Gasparinisaura en el taxón Euiguanodontia

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses suggest that Anabisetia may be positioned just outside Iguanodontia, similar to its relative Gasparinisaura.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en recientes análisis cladísticos realizados por Coria y otros colaboradores, colocan a Gasparinisaura justo por fuera de Iguanodontia

facts.statement: In 2015, Anabisetia was found to belong to the clade Elasmaria along with other ornithopods from Antarctica and Patagonia.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2015, se encontró que los dos taxones son parte del clado Elasmaria junto con otros ornitópodos de la Antártida y la Patagonia

facts.statement: Anabisetia is a member of the parent group Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmaria

facts.statement: Anabisetia is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Anabisetia lived during the Turonian stage, approximately 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Anabisetia in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

rejected.statement: The species A. saldiviai is named after Roberto Saldivia Blanco, a local farmer who discovered the fossils in 1985.
rejected.quote: The one named species is called A. saldiviai, after Roberto Saldivia Blanco, a local farmer who had discovered the fossils in 1985 and brought them to the attention of science in 1993.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'after Roberto Saldivia Blanco a local farmer who'

rejected.statement: All four known specimens were found at Cerro Bayo Mesa, 30 km south of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
rejected.quote: All four specimens were discovered at a locality called Cerro Bayo Mesa, thirty kilometers south of Plaza Huincul in the Neuquén province of Argentina.

rejected.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Anabisetia's weight at 20 kilograms in 2010.
rejected.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at two meters, its weight at twenty kilograms.

rejected.statement: Anabisetia saldiviai was a small, running herbivore approximately 2 meters long, 60 cm high, and weighing 20 kg.
rejected.quote: Anabisetia saldiviai fue un pequeño herbívoro corredor de aproximadamente dos metros de largo, 60 centímetros de alto y un peso estimado de 20 kilogramos.
